key_insight: Chest X-ray foundation models that perform well on adult data lose substantial accuracy when applied to pediatric cases, showing poor cross-population generalization under domain shift.
clinical_relevance: For AI-assisted chest X-ray triage or screening, pediatric deployment may require separate validation and adaptation rather than assuming adult-trained models will transfer reliably.
method: Harmonized VinDr-CXR and PediCXR into a 5-label chest X-ray classification benchmark.
Compared 6 foundation models and 2 CNN baselines.
Tested linear probing, partial fine-tuning, and full fine-tuning using adult data for adaptation only.
evidence_signal: Across the benchmark, Macro-AUROC was about 92% on adult test data but dropped to around 78% on pediatric data, with declines exceeding 10 percentage points for all models.
watch_item: Strong adult in-domain performance did not predict pediatric success, and deeper fine-tuning did not meaningfully fix the transfer gap.
paper_title: From Adults to Children: Benchmarking Foundation Models for Chest X-Ray Classification under Domain Shift
